key_insight: The paper shows that in covert multi-AUV missions, communication should be optimized for the task value of sensed information rather than for idealized message exchange.
engineering_relevance: This matters for underwater robotics because it can improve cooperative performance while reducing acoustic transmissions, delay, and exposure risk under realistic covert constraints.
method: Introduces SVR-MARL to measure the realized task utility of sensed information.
Uses distributed MARL to learn cooperative policies from practical, imperfect observations.
Applies the framework to covert multi-AUV localization and tracking with communication constraints.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a case study on covert multi-AUV cooperative localization and tracking demonstrating improved task efficiency with less unnecessary communication and exposure risk.
watch_item: Performance may depend on how well the sensed-information value model matches real underwater conditions, which can be difficult to estimate reliably.
paper_title: Task-Oriented Sensing and Covert Transmissions for Collaborative Multi-AUV Systems
